q1.explanationZh: 女孩说堂兄把旧吉他送给了她，她打算自学吉他。A 错：妈妈说打鼓太吵，邻居会抱怨；C 错：姐姐弹钢琴，她不太想模仿姐姐。

q2.explanationZh: 男孩想看古典音乐节目，因为对他下周要交的课题很有用；女孩觉得这是重要的事，就同意了。A 错：访谈节目是昨晚看的；C 错：女孩本想看足球赛，但最后让步了。

q3.explanationZh: 女孩说右边的是堂兄 Jerry，他和平时一样穿着 T 恤，是唯一这么穿的人，两个男孩都穿运动鞋。B 右边男孩穿的是连帽衫；C 右边男孩穿的是毛衣和靴子。

q4.explanationZh: 男孩说疼的地方比膝盖低，更像是脚踝而不是脚后跟。A 指的是膝盖；C 指的是脚后跟。

q5.explanationZh: 老师建议带 12 英镑现金：午饭约 8 英镑，剩下的钱可以在商店买东西。A 错：8 英镑只够午饭；C 错：24 英镑是已经交过的车费和门票钱。

q6.explanationZh: 老师说照片上这种蝴蝶每个翅膀上有两个挨在一起的斑点（two spots next to each other, like this one）。A 是她提到的另一种只有一个斑点的蝴蝶；B 是下节课才会看到的蝴蝶。

q7.explanationZh: 女孩说上次做的是苹果派（The last thing we did was apple pie）。B 错：巧克力蛋糕要过几节课才学；C 错：巧克力曲奇是这周要学的。

q8.explanationZh: 女孩说物理是一门很棒的学科，她学到了很多。A 错：她想加入帮助送宇航员上太空的研究团队，不是想当宇航员；B 错：她说科幻片不真实，她看的多是纪录片。

q9.explanationZh: 男孩说国际象棋很复杂，女孩说自己一开始也很难弄懂，两人都认为它不容易学。A 错：男孩觉得它有趣；C 错：女孩只提到一款教下棋的电脑游戏，并没有比较哪个更好玩。

q10.explanationZh: 女士说她原以为汉堡会很大（would be enormous），言下之意是比预想的小。B 错：男士说价格便宜；C 错：她说汉堡和菜单图片上看起来一样好吃。

q11.explanationZh: 女孩说要先读很多历史资料，不确定下周末前能否完成，可见作业量很大。B 错：她说主要的写作练习看起来不难；C 错：她说自己能独立完成。

q12.explanationZh: 女孩说那么多优秀的游泳选手参加选拔，她从没想过会被选上，所以感到意外。A 错：需要时老师会额外辅导她，没问题；C 错：她只是说比赛很多，并不困惑。

q13.explanationZh: 男孩说如果去离学校更近的河，在那里的时间会更长，说明他觉得这条河太远了。A 错：他说 10 英镑玩一整天不算贵；C 错：他觉得是女孩不喜欢早起，而不是他自己。

q14.explanationZh: 当地人因为海鹦的颜色叫它们“海鹦鹉”（sea parrots）；她自己觉得它们像小丑。

q15.explanationZh: 海鹦在陆地上（On land）走路的样子有点傻，人们看了会笑；在水里它们游得很快。

q16.explanationZh: 冬天（In the winter）海鹦会飞向大海，直到第二年春天才再出现；5 月到 7 月是繁殖期。

q17.explanationZh: 海鹦像兔子一样（just like rabbits）在地里筑巢。

q18.explanationZh: 去年岛上有将近 80,000 只海鹦；100,000 是以前一些年份的数量。

q19.explanationZh: 人们不能离海鹦太近，但一直需要志愿者去清点（count）它们的数量。

q20.explanationZh: Jennifer 在一场名人喜剧演出中和一位明星聊天，给他讲了个笑话，他笑了，这让她有了信心。A 错：在学校演出是那之后的事；C 错：她不确定家人笑是不是只为了让她开心。

q21.explanationZh: 她说最能逗笑观众的，是把自己身上发生的日常小事稍加改编。A、B 错：看电视新闻编笑话、别人建议的方法对她都不管用。

q22.explanationZh: 同学们很高兴身边有一个会讲喜剧的人，喜欢向朋友们介绍她，说明为她骄傲。A 错：没说同学想学这些技能；C 错：同学们说早就料到她会成功，感到意外的是她自己。

q23.explanationZh: 她说有一次想不起下一个笑话是什么，场面一度尴尬地冷场。B 错：有人喊 Hurry up! 只是因为她忘词，且她用一句妙语化解了；C 错：观众不笑的情况她认为将来会发生，目前还没发生过。

q24.explanationZh: 她说看观众的反应能直接告诉她笑话好不好笑，这比什么都更能促使她进步。A 错：老师不是喜剧演员，很难帮她提高；B 错：她只是从电影里的喜剧演员那里得到一些灵感。

q25.explanationZh: 她说太喜欢演出了，不会彻底放弃（give them up totally），会继续表演。B 错：当医生是她小时候的梦想；C 错：她觉得如果当成职业就不好玩了。

content.v: Test Four. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now, because you must not speak during the test.
Now look at the instructions for Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. Which instrument is the girl going to learn to play?
Hi Fran. Last time I saw you, you were thinking about taking up a musical instrument, but you weren’t sure which one. Have you decided yet?

Well, my sister plays the piano. I’m not sure I’d really want to copy her though. My cousin’s just given me his old guitar, so I thought I’d try and teach myself that. I did wonder about the drums, but my mum says they’d be too loud and the neighbours would complain.
Sounds good; let me know when your first concert is!
Two. Which programme are they going to watch?
The soccer game starts soon, doesn’t it?
You want to watch that?
Well yeah ... of course I do!

I was kind of hoping to watch that programme on classical music. It’d be really useful for my project that’s due next week, and Mum’ll get mad if you don’t let me. And don’t forget that last night I let you watch that stupid chat show you love.
Um, well as it’s for something important, go on then. And what do you mean you let me? You love it too ... you know you do!
Three. Which picture shows the girl’s cousin?
Is that your cousin you’re standing next to in this photo? The boy in the trainers?
Well both boys are wearing trainers. Look... But yes, that’s Jerry on the right.
Oh right. Sorry. Wasn’t he cold? I mean, you said you felt so cold you had no choice but to put on your warm sweatshirt and boots!
He never seems to feel the cold. He wore a T-shirt as usual. But he was the only one dressed like that. Nearly everyone else had a sweater at least.
Four. Which part of the boy’s leg is painful?
Hello Edward. My name’s Nurse Brown. I’m the school nurse. I believe you’ve hurt your leg. Is that right?
Yes.
Alright. Can I have a look? I can see it’s a bit red. What happened?
Well I was playing football with the others and then I fell over.
But your knee’s not hurting?
The pain’s lower down than that.
Is it here?
It’s more my ankle rather than my heel. It really hurts and it’s hard to walk.
Yes, I can see why.
Five. How much money should students take on the trip?

OK, listen carefully to the information about Saturday’s trip to the Adventure Park. Now you’ve all paid your twenty four pounds, which covers the bus fare and your entrance ticket to the park itself. Once you’re inside the park all the rides are free. However, I do recommend you bring twelve pounds in cash. If you eat in the café there, lunch is around eight pounds – including drinks and an ice cream. So after that, you’ll still have some money to spend in the shop before we leave.
Six. Which picture is the teacher talking about?

Look at this photo. This species of Wall Butterfly is lovely, isn’t it? There’s another kind with just one spot at the top of each wing. The ones with two spots next to each other, like this one, are more common in warmer climates. This one’s very rare in this country. I’ve only seen them once or twice myself. In our next lesson, about South America, you’ll see a similar type of butterfly – one with spots on the top and the bottom of its wings. It’s also really beautiful!
Seven. What has the girl learned how to make?
How are your cooking classes at school going?
Great, thanks. We’ve just moved on to making desserts – my favourite.
So what are you making?

Well, chocolate cake’s definitely one of the things on the list I’m most looking forward to, but that’s not for a few lessons. The last thing we did was apple pie, which was harder than I thought it’d be. And we’re learning to cook chocolate chip biscuits this week. I’ll save one for you to try after the lesson.
That’d be great, thanks.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear two friends talking about their school project.
What do you think about the project we’re doing on space at school?
It’s okay. What about you?
It’s my favourite topic of the year so far!
Why’s that?
Well, one day I’d like to be part of a research team that helps send astronauts into space. Physics is such an amazing subject. I’m learning so much.
I suppose so. I can see why you’re enjoying the project so much. I’ve watched a lot of films about space travel.
Really? Most science fiction movies are hardly realistic, so the sort of stuff I watch is mostly documentaries.
Oh, right.
Nine. You will hear two friends talking during a game of chess.
I know you’ve only played chess once before, but you should know you can’t do that.
Why not? I thought it was a good move.
Yes, but you’re not allowed to move that piece like that. Only the one that looks like a horse can jump over other pieces.
Really? It’s so complicated – but I suppose that’s what makes it interesting. I need a lot more practice though.
I had trouble understanding everything at first too, but then Dad showed me this brilliant computer game which teaches you all about chess in a really entertaining way. You should try it.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking in a fast food restaurant.
I really love eating here. The food’s great – and isn’t that expensive either.
Well yeah, that’s true I suppose. This burger’s as delicious as it looks in the picture on the menu.
And it’s really good value, I think. Look at this huge pile of chips – fantastic!
Yeah, but I thought my burger would be enormous. I mean, compare that to the amount of chips you got.
Oh stop complaining, and have some of my chips. And anyway, at these prices you could always buy yourself another one.
I suppose you’re right. Okay – give me some chips then.
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about their history homework.
Have you done your history homework yet?
No, not yet. I’ve had a look at it, but to be honest I’ve not even started it yet. I’m not sure I’ll get it done by the end of next week.
You sound worried. I thought you really liked history! Why don’t we do it together in the library?

I think I’ll manage on my own actually. The main writing exercise doesn’t seem very hard – it’ll be quite interesting too. It’s just that there are so many historical texts to read first, but if you need a hand, I’ll give you some advice.
Twelve. You will hear a girl talking to a friend about becoming a member of a swimming team.
I hear they’ve accepted you for the school swimming team. I knew you’d do it. Why didn’t you believe me?
There were loads of good swimmers trying for it so I never thought they’d select me. I’ve got training at least three times a week. I’ve no idea how I’ll find time.
What about schoolwork?

They said I’ll get extra help from my teachers if I need it, so it’ll be fine. But I wonder when I’ll get to see my friends at weekends if I’m always going to competitions. There are going to be so many this term.
Thirteen. You will hear two friends talking about a school trip to a river.
Have you seen the details about the class trip next month? To a river, so we’ll learn more about them.
Yes, we’ll have to get up at 5 o’clock if the coach goes at 6. You won’t like that!
I don’t mind, if it means we’ll have as much time as possible at the river.
We’d have even longer if we went to one that’s closer to school.
But there aren’t any near here, and we want an adventure! Anyway, it’s only £10 to go.
I suppose that’s not too much for a full day out. And food’s included!
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a student giving a talk about a trip to see some seabirds called puffins.
Last weekend, I went with my family to some islands off the coast to see some seabirds called puffins.

These birds are really cute. Their beaks are orange, grey and yellow, and their bodies are black and white. The people around there call them sea parrots. It’s because of their colours, but puffins actually make me think of clowns.

People sometimes laugh at puffins when they see the way they walk. On land they look a bit silly – but in the water they swim very fast. You can find some great videos online that show how they use their wings when they’re flying in the air.

We went out on a boat to the islands to see the puffins. Their breeding season’s from May to July. That’s when they have their babies. In the winter they go out to sea and they aren’t seen again until the following spring.

Puffins make nests for their babies in the ground, just like rabbits do. It means you can’t see the babies, but when they do come out of the nest, the adult puffins have to make sure the babies aren’t caught by bigger seabirds or rats.

Puffin numbers have been falling on the islands due to fishing and climate change, which is a real shame. Last year, there were nearly 80,000 on the islands. This was the same number as the previous year, but lower than other years, when around 100,000 arrived.

You can’t get too close to the puffins as it can scare them. But volunteers are always needed to count them. I’d love to help with that! Also, if you’re interested in photography, you might get close enough to them to photograph them more easily.
If you want to go and see the puffins ... [fade]
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four.
For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a girl called Jennifer Marsden, who is a comedian, someone who tells jokes in front of an audience.
Jennifer, you’re only sixteen but have already taken part in several comedy shows. When did you first realise you were good at telling jokes?

I’ve always tried to make people laugh. At home, though, I was never sure if everyone was laughing to keep me happy, or if my jokes were actually funny. This changed when I went to a big-name comedy show and chatted with one of the stars. I tried one of my jokes on him and he laughed, which gave me enough confidence to try performing in a school show.
How do you write your funniest jokes?

Well, what seems to get the most laughs is when I take day-to-day things that have happened to me and change them a bit so they’re funnier. Any technique suggested by someone else, like seeing the news on TV and creating jokes based on that, has never worked well for me.
What do your classmates at school think about you being a comedian?

A lot of them are creative, but because nobody else does comedy they’re pleased to have someone they know who’s got those skills. It’s good for the school and my classmates like telling their friends about me. They all say they expected me to do well, which I find surprising.
What do you find most difficult when you’re on stage?

The hardest thing for any comedian is when an audience doesn’t find you funny – I’m sure that’ll happen to me one day. Once, I couldn’t remember which joke came next, so there was a long embarrassing silence. Someone said ‘Hurry up!’ really loudly, which made me think of a funny reply that made everyone laugh.
Who has helped you develop as a comedian most?

My teachers have been fantastic in encouraging me. As they’re not comedians, though, it’s hard for them to help me improve. Seeing how the audience reacts tells me directly whether my material’s working or not, which has pushed me to do better more than anything else. I pick up ideas watching my favourite comedians in films too.
Do you want a career in comedy in the future?

When I was younger, I used to dream of being a doctor – I liked the idea of helping people. Obviously comedy helps people – it’s good for us to laugh – but I think it would stop being fun if it was my job. I enjoy the shows too much to give them up totally, but I’d rather do something else.
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
